content.text: I've reviewed the full document (all four substantive sections and the fee, exclusivity, cross-promotion and general provisions). No MFN-type obligation runs against the Company.

input.quote: 1.8 HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on the Company. The fee provisions (§ 3.1–3.4) fix a flat 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold with no obligation to extend HDI any better terms offered to third parties or to match third-party offers. The only "no less favorably" covenant runs against HDI (§ 1.8: HDI must promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than its own catalog titles), and the cross-promotion covenant in § 7.1 is mutual and "reciprocal and equitable" rather than an MFN in HDI's favour, so neither is flagged. The exclusivity covenant in § 6.1 restricts the Company's competing web projects but is not a pricing/terms MFN and is addressed under the exclusivity rule, not here. This meets the preferred position: no Customer MFN benefiting the Vendor, and the provisions that lean one way lean in our favour, so no redline is proposed.
